events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
FFWRLX

The National Weather Service in Charleston has extended the

* Flash Flood Warning for...
Northern Roane County in central West Virginia...
Calhoun County in north central West Virginia...
Gilmer County in north central West Virginia...
Southwestern Doddridge County in northern West Virginia...
Northeastern Jackson County in northwestern West Virginia...
Southern Ritchie County in northwestern West Virginia...
Wirt County in northwestern West Virginia...
Southeastern Wood County in northwestern West Virginia...

* Until 900 AM EDT.

* At 714 AM EDT, Doppler radar and automated rain gauges indicated
thunderstorms producing heavy rain across the warned area. Between
1.5 and 2.5 inches of rain have fallen. Additional rainfall amounts
up to 1 inch are possible in the warned area. Flash flooding is
ongoing or expected to begin shortly.

HAZARD...Flash flooding caused by thunderstorms.

SOURCE...Radar and automated gauges.

IMPACT...Flash flooding of small creeks and streams, urban areas,
highways, streets and underpasses as well as other poor
drainage and low-lying areas.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Spencer, Glenville, Elizabeth, Grantsville, Arnoldsburg, Cedar
Creek State Park, Reedy, Sand Fork, Pullman, Auburn, Munday,
Annamoriah, Brohard, Creston, Macfarlan, Big Springs, Mount Zion,
Smithville, Cherry, and Millstone.

This includes Interstate 77 in West Virginia near mile marker 150...
and between mile markers 152 and 163.

events.region: Cedar, IA; Iowa, IA; Johnson, IA; Keokuk, IA; Louisa, IA; Muscatine, IA; Washington, IA
events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
FFWDVN

The National Weather Service in Quad Cities has extended the

* Flash Flood Warning for...
Southern Cedar County in east central Iowa...
Iowa County in east central Iowa...
Johnson County in east central Iowa...
Muscatine County in east central Iowa...
Keokuk County in southeastern Iowa...
Northwestern Louisa County in southeastern Iowa...
Washington County in southeastern Iowa...

* Until 815 AM CDT.

* At 541 AM CDT, Trained weather spotters reported flash flooding in
Kalona. Between 2 and 4 inches of rain have fallen across portions
of the warned area. Flash flooding is ongoing. Rain has tapered off
to mainly light to at times moderate rain, with the heaviest rain
having already occurred. Be alert for rapid rises and flooding on
area streams, creeks and along the English River. Washington County
deputies reported around a foot of water was covering the
intersection of 133rd Street and Nutmeg Street in Kalona due to the
English River being out its banks.

HAZARD...Flash flooding caused by thunderstorms.

SOURCE...Trained spotters reported.

IMPACT...Flash flooding of small creeks and streams, urban areas,
highways, streets and underpasses as well as other poor
drainage and low-lying areas.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Iowa City, Muscatine, Washington, Tipton, Marengo, West Branch,
Sigourney, Columbus Junction, Durant, Coralville, North Liberty,
West Liberty, Williamsburg, Wilton, Kalona, Tiffin, Wellman, Lone
Tree and University Heights.

This includes the following highways...
Interstate 80 in Iowa between mile markers 205 and 277. Interstate
380 between mile markers 1 and 7.

events.region: Musselshell; Treasure; Northern Rosebud; Custer; Fallon; Powder River; Carter; Northern Big Horn; Southern Rosebud; Southern Big Horn; Bighorn Canyon; Pryor/Northern Bighorn Mountains; Northeastern Yellowstone; Southwestern Yellowstone; Northeast Bighorn Mountains; Sheridan Foothills
events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
Showers are turning light and tapering off along the western
foothills, but healthier showers will continue over central and
eastern portions of the forecast area today. The risk of flooding
continues.

* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is possible, along
with flash flooding over recent burn scars.

* WHERE...Southeast Montana and Sheridan County Wyoming.

* WHEN...Through this afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of creeks and
other low-lying and flood-prone locations. Flooding may occur in
poor drainage and urban areas. The risk of flooding will diminish
late this afternoon and evening as showers taper off.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- The heaviest rainfall is slowly shifting eastward to southeast
Montana and northeast Wyoming.
- The Elk and McGhee-Remington burn scars are particularly
vulnerable to flash flooding and debris flows. Any other burn
scars from this summer will have elevated flash flood potential
as well.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
